result.rationale: Fresh, pea-sized, superficial abrasion already cleaned and covered, with no bleeding, warmth, swelling, drainage, or systemic symptoms. Diabetes raises the stakes for foot wounds, so guidance should include daily inspection, avoiding the offending shoe/pressure on the heel, keeping it clean and covered, and prompt clinician contact if redness, warmth, swelling, drainage, pain, fever, or lack of healing within about a week appears (sooner if the patient has known neuropathy or poor circulation), but no clinician assessment is needed now.
